answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted peer attestation with slow identity accrual. A newcomer posts a bond and must be attested by established peers before its votes count, so a thousand fresh keys anchored on one cheap reef of identities still sit at zero trust. Reputation accrues as sand piles on a dune: only through sustained, verifiable work, so fabricating it burns real compute and time. The karst channels between long-lived peers form over months and cannot be drilled overnight, which makes mass identity fraud expensive, not merely inconvenient.
